🇲🇽🏭 <u>NEARSHORING KEEPS LANDING: PLANT INAUGURATIONS TRIPLE IN MEXICO</u>

Yes, new investment announcements fell nearly 80% in the first quarter as companies wait out the T-MEC review. But the money committed in previous years is turning into steel and jobs: "In inaugurations we're seeing almost triple what we saw last year," Integralia analyst Alberto Quiroz told El Economista.

The evidence runs along the Bajío-to-border corridor: Airbus opened a $35.8 million plant in Colón, Querétaro; Clarios a $147 million automated center in Torreón moving 11 million batteries a year; Baltimore Aircoil its first Latin America plant in Nuevo León ($100 million, 500 jobs); China's Zoomlion its Latin American agri-machinery hub in Aguascalientes.

Announcements are headlines. Inaugurations are production.

🇲🇽⚓ <u>"MEXICO BELIEVES IN YOU, MEXICO TRUSTS YOU": SHEINBAUM TO 211 NEW NAVY OFFICERS</u>

President Claudia Sheinbaum presided over the graduation of 211 guardiamarinas of the Heroica Escuela Naval Militar in Alvarado, Veracruz — 170 fleet officers, 27 marines and 14 naval pilots, including a record 73 women, the most ever to graduate from the institution.

"Mexico believes in you, Mexico trusts you, Mexico knows that when it needs you, you will be there — as the sailors of our homeland have always been," the Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces told them. "You carry on your shoulders the responsibility of defending sovereignty."

🇲🇽🇵🇸 <u>MEXICANS MARCH AGAINST PAN GOVERNOR'S WATER DEAL WITH ISRAEL</u>

From Chihuahua and Ciudad Juárez to the Ángel de la Independencia in Mexico City, protesters demanded the cancellation of the water cooperation deal between Chihuahua's water board and Mashav — Israel's state cooperation agency — signed in 2023, valid until 2027 and never registered with Mexico's Foreign Ministry.

Marches also hit Puebla, Monterrey, Saltillo, Pachuca, Toluca, Aguascalientes and Querétaro, with demands for a Gaza ceasefire and an end to commercial ties with Israel.

"Who decides over Chihuahua's water, and under what interests?" asked Salvemos los Cerros, accusing PAN governor Maru Campos of doing business with a government committing genocide.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>MICHOACÁN: ARMY TAKES DOWN CARTEL BOSS THE U.S. HAD A $5M BOUNTY ON</u>

Mexico's Army detained Alfonso "Poncho La Quiringua" Fernández Magallón, boss of the Cártel de Los Reyes, in Imbarácuaro, Michoacán — a man U.S. authorities offered up to $5 million for, accused of drone attacks on Mexican soldiers in Cotija, Tingüindín and Jacona.

The cartel's answer was five roadblocks and burning vehicles in Los Reyes and Peribán. Security forces had them cleared within five hours. He now sits in FGR facilities in Mexico City.

Mexican intelligence, Mexican operation, Mexican results.

‍VOZ.US: Mexican Army arrests leader of Cartel de los Reyes, for whom the US had offered a $5 million reward August 2, 2026 | 🟢 📰 The Mexican Army captured Alfonso Fernández Magallón, alleged Cartel de los Reyes leader with a $5M US bounty, in Michoacán. The cartel answered with roadblocks and burning vehicles; security held. The US ambassador's response: a round of applause and a shared-commitment quote. 🇲🇽 Straight AFP-based write-up from a conservative US outlet — credit goes to Mexico's army and security cabinet, not Washington. • "set up roadblocks and set vehicles on fire" • "criminals have nowhere to hide"

text: ‍AP/US NEWS: Trump Administration Pushes Tougher English Rules for Mexican Train Crews Crossing Into the US July 31, 2026 | 🟡 📰 New FRA rule caps Mexican train crews at 10 miles inside the US over English proficiency. 🇲🇽🏭 <u>J.P. MORGAN: T-MEC RENEWAL WILL BE SIGNED — BUT NOT UNTIL NEXT YEAR</u>

“Everything is being configured” as a T-MEC renegotiation that stretches into 2027, says Gabriel Lozano, J.P. Morgan’s chief economist for Mexico — but the bank expects the renewal to be signed.

His warning: Mexico is riding the tech boom in non-auto manufacturing, yet without closing gaps in energy, water, connectivity and human capital it risks remaining the assembler while the US keeps the data centers and semiconductors. “Mexico has to demonstrate it can make a greater contribution to the world economy, precisely because of the productive chains it has with the United States and Canada.” (El Economista)
